hypothesis: Fine-tuning the current DeepFM+numeric+session champion with a warm-started, staged within-user BPR pairwise loss (pointwise pretrain to convergence as now, then continue optimizing purely on sampled within-user positive/negative pairs, keeping the best-of-either checkpoint) will push GAUC/nDCG@5 further because it directly targets the ranking objective without the hybrid-loss interference that hurt a prior attempt.
change_spec: 1. Keep encode()/build_numeric()/FIELDS/M_NUM exactly as in the current champion (7 categorical fields incl. hour/session buckets, 11 numeric priors incl. user-tab rate and log1p counts) -- no feature changes. 2. Add a new training stage in train_deepfm-style flow: (a) train the full DeepFM exactly as today (pointwise BCE) to its early-stopped best state -- call this the pretrain stage, unchanged code path, tag='pretrain'. (b) Build pair pools ONCE (not per epoch): for the TRAIN split only, group row indices by user_id; for every user with >=1 positive AND >=1 negative row in train, store pos_idx array and neg_idx array (numpy int arrays). Concatenate all users' arrays into two big index arrays pos_all, neg_all via vectorized construction (no per-user Python loop over rows -- only a loop over the ~26k distinct users to fill lists, then np.concatenate once; this is a one-time O(n_users) build, not O(rows) per epoch). (c) Each fine-tune epoch: resample neg_all by drawing a fresh random negative index from the SAME user's neg-index array for every pos row (vectorized via array indexing with random column selection per user, or oversample pos_all K=2x by repeating and drawing random negatives) -- must be pure numpy indexing, no Python row loop. (d) New method DeepFM.step_pairwise(Xpos,Zpos,Xneg,Zneg): compute z_pos,*_ = self.logits(Xpos,Zpos) and z_neg,*_ = self.logits(Xneg,Zneg) in one forward each (reuse existing logits()); let d = sigmoid(z_neg - z_pos) (vector over the pair batch); this is dL/dz_pos = -d and dL/dz_neg = +d for L=-log(sigmoid(z_pos-z_neg)). Build a combined batch of concatenated pos and neg rows (X_cat=[Xpos;Xneg], Z_cat=[Zpos;Zneg]) with per-row gradient g_cat=[-d/B; +d/B], and call the EXACT same accumulation/backward code path used in step() (gV/gW/MLP backward) but substitute g_cat for the BCE gradient g -- do not rederive the FM math, just replace the gradient vector's source terms in a refactored helper shared by step() and step_pairwise(). Same Adam state, LR=0.001, L2=1e-6. 3. Fine-tune schedule: start from the pretrain best_state (warm start), run up to 8 epochs of step_pairwise over resampled pairs, batch=8192 pairs, evaluate validation primary via evaluate() each epoch exactly as now, keep the OVERALL best state across BOTH pretrain and fine-tune epochs (patience=3 on the fine-tune stage; if fine-tune never beats the pretrain best, keep the pretrain model -- this makes the stage strictly non-regressive by construction). Print pair_count and per-epoch primary as today's logging format. 4. Riders: after selecting the best single model, run this same pretrain+fine-tune pipeline for seeds 0,1,2 and average their validation/target predictions (rank-safe score average, 3-seed ensemble) as the FULL bundle written to preds.csv -- this is the validated variance-reduction rider from prior runs. 5. Ablations to print: 'champion_equiv' = today's pointwise-only DeepFM+numeric+session, single seed, subsampled as currently coded (already exists, keep it); 'bpr_finetune_1seed' = the pretrain+BPR-finetune pipeline with seed=0 only, no ensembling, scored on FULL validation (not subsampled) so it is directly comparable to 'full'; 'full' = the 3-seed-averaged bundle. 6. Runtime: pretrain ~45-55s/seed (unchanged), fine-tune ~8 epochs * ~1.5-2s pair batches ~15s/seed, so ~70s/seed * 3 seeds ~210s, plus champion_equiv/no_confidence_counts/no_session_fields ablations at reduced rows (~60s total) -- total well under the 1500s wall-clock budget. 7. Leave CLI, output format, train-only rule, and past-only feature computation unchanged; do NOT use any same-row feedback column in step_pairwise beyond the label used to build the pos/neg index split (label used only to partition indices before training, never as an input feature).
rationale: Rendle et al. UAI 2009 (BPR) and Uematsu & Lee 2017 establish that pairwise ranking losses are calibrated for AUC-type metrics, which matches GAUC directly; this dataset's negatives are observed impressions (not missing data), so uniform within-user pair sampling is well-founded per the survey evidence cited in the knowledge library §8.1. The ledger shows this exact mechanism worked three times when applied as the primary loss (not hybridized), and failed once specifically as a hybrid addition on this run's champion -- the staged warm-start design directly targets that documented failure mode rather than re-testing it unchanged.
gain_evidence: Cross-run ledger (PRIOR RUNS table) shows three separate measurements of full within-user BPR loss replacing pointwise BCE: +0.0029, +0.0018, +0.0012, all promoted -- a consistently positive mechanism when implemented as the primary loss with warm-up rather than a simultaneous hybrid. The one negative result in the ledger (-0.0012, kept_champion) was specifically a HYBRID weighted-sum of BPR+BCE added on top of this run's exact champion architecture, which is the failure mode this spec avoids by staging (pretrain fully, then fine-tune purely on pairs, keeping whichever checkpoint scores higher). Calibration in this run has run +0.0042 high on average, so I am predicting below the largest prior BPR delta (+0.0029) to account for a stronger starting champion having less headroom; 3-seed ensembling is a separately validated rider (+0.0002 to +00017 across multiple prior runs) stacked as insurance.
ablation_plan: champion_equiv: current pointwise-only DeepFM+numeric+session (no BPR stage), subsampled as today; bpr_finetune_1seed: the pretrain+BPR-finetune pipeline at seed=0 only (no ensembling), scored on full validation to isolate the loss effect from the ensembling effect; full: the 3-seed-averaged bpr_finetune bundle (the proposed champion).
search_check: Direction considered: within-user pairwise BPR loss with warm-start staging (Rendle et al., UAI 2009), applied as a training-objective change rather than a new architecture. BPR is a 15-year-old, closed-form pairwise ranking loss with no active research controversy about its core mechanics; I already have three internal measured positive deltas and one measured negative (hybrid variant) from this project's own ledger, which is stronger, more relevant evidence than a generic literature search would add for deciding the implementation variant (staged vs hybrid) -- the fix is derived from my own prior measurements, not from new published work.
